questions.text: A Buddhist temple monument features 5 or 7 diminishing floor levels, domed roofs, radiating eaves supported by elaborate wooden brackets, and often houses no relics or statuary—standing as a sculptural monument rather than a functional religious space. This describes which structure type?

options.text: Stupa (Buddhist relic dome) with a solid core and circumambulatory path
Shikhara (Hindu temple tower) characterized by its vertical emphasis and ornate carvings
Pagoda (Japanese Buddhist monument)
Gopura (Hindu gateway tower) serving as an entrance to temple complexes

rationale.a: Stupa is a hemispherical dome, not a multi-story tapering tower.
rationale.b: Shikhara is a Hindu tower, not a Buddhist monument.
rationale.d: Gopura is a Hindu gateway, not a Buddhist vertical monument.
rationale.correct: Pagoda is explicitly defined as a vertical Buddhist monument typically 5 or 7 stories with diminishing floor levels, domed roofs, and radiating eaves. Unlike Chinese equivalents, Japanese pagodas often house no relics—they stand as sculptural monuments.
rationale.takeaway: Unlike Chinese equivalents, Japanese pagodas often house no relics—they stand as sculptural monuments.

Japanese architecture simply copies Chinese designs without modification, which overlooks significant adaptations

Shikinen Sengu is performed only on damaged structures; Western restoration maintains buildings indefinitely regardless of condition.
